title: What's Included in an Egypt Day Tour (and What Isn't)
excerpt: Egypt day tour inclusions explained: guide, transport, entry tickets, hotel pickup and lunch, plus the extras you pay for. Real Sawa tour lists, from €29.
body_html:
Prices, timetables and visiting details are a November 2026 snapshot. Check the linked official pages and your departure’s current inclusions and terms before booking.

Quick answer

A typical Egypt day tour includes a licensed guide, air-conditioned transport, hotel pickup and drop-off, and entrance tickets to the sites named in the itinerary. Some full-day tours add lunch, and some list taxes and service charges. It usually excludes tips, drinks, camel rides, inside-pyramid and special-tomb tickets, and anything optional that the itinerary does not name. The only reliable test is the tour page's own included and not-included lists, which is why this post walks through three real ones.

Check current UK government travel advice for Egypt before making your arrangements; advice can change.

You spot two Luxor day tours at different prices and no way to tell what is in either. Day tour inclusions follow a pattern across the market, yet few pages spell them out, so travellers get caught out by tickets, lunches and tips they assumed were covered. This post lists what a shared Egypt day tour usually includes, what it usually does not, and how pickup works, using Sawa's own pages as the worked examples. Sawa Tours (sawa.tours), the Egypt shared-departure platform, publishes the included and not-included lists on its tour pages, and our founder has worked in Egyptian tourism since 1993.

Egypt day tour inclusions: what's usually in the price

Four things appear on the Sawa day tours we checked (8 November 2026): a licensed guide, an air-conditioned vehicle, hotel pickup and drop-off, and entrance tickets for the sites on the itinerary. Those four are the core of the price: what makes the day a tour rather than a taxi with commentary. Taxes and service charges are named as included on the Giza Uncovered page.

The guide matters most. Egyptian law requires tour guides to hold a Ministry licence (Law 121 of 1983), every guided Sawa tour has a licensed guide, and on a shared departure one guide stays with the group from pickup to drop-off. The tour is operated by one of the licensed Egyptian agencies with travellers on the date, registered with ETAA and named before your deposit is due.

Transport and pickup travel together: an air-conditioned vehicle collects you at your hotel and returns you there at the end. Hotel pickup and drop-off are listed on Giza Uncovered, the four-hour pyramids tour (from €29), on Luxor in Depth (from €75) and on the nine-hour Aswan to Abu Simbel trip (from €50), all per person, as listed in November 2026.

What's usually not included in the price

The standard exclusions are gratuities, drinks and bottled water, camel rides, entrance inside the pyramids, special tombs, and any optional activity not named in the itinerary. These are not surprises on a well-listed page, but they are the items travellers most often assume are covered.

Usually included Usually not included
Licensed guide Gratuities for guide and driver (tipping)
Hotel pickup and drop-off Drinks and bottled water
Air-conditioned transport Camel rides at Giza
Entrance tickets to itinerary sites Inside-pyramid tickets (Khufu and others)
Lunch on some full-day tours (check the list) Special tombs: Tutankhamun, Nefertari
Taxes and service charges (where listed) Personal expenses and shopping
Optional activities not listed as included

Tipping, known locally as baksheesh (a small cash gift for service), is the exclusion that catches most visitors out. Gratuities are on the not-included lists of Luxor in Depth, the Grand West Bank, Aswan to Abu Simbel and the Nile cruises; the Giza Uncovered list does not mention them, but nothing is bundled there either. Guides and drivers in Egypt rely on tips as part of their income. Budget cash for them, per person, per day: 2026 guides quote about EGP 100 to 200 per person (about €2 to €3 at EGP 60 to the euro, 8 November 2026) for a group guide on a full-day tour, with higher figures from operators who quote in dollars (Egypt Tours Plus, October 2026).

Lunch varies by tour, so read the list. Giza Uncovered, about four hours, says "Meals and drinks not mentioned" under not included. Aswan to Abu Simbel, about nine hours, lists "Lunch at a local restaurant en route" as included, as does the Grand West Bank. Luxor in Depth mentions a local-restaurant lunch en route in its itinerary but not in either list, so check the departure page before you rely on it. Drinks at any lunch, bottled water included, are normally paid separately.

The one-line rule: if an item is not on the included list, assume you pay for it on the day. Included lists are generous but exact: they describe your tour, not a category of tours.

How hotel pickup and meeting points work

Hotel pickup and drop-off are listed on the Sawa day tours we checked: Giza Uncovered collects from Cairo and Giza hotels, Luxor in Depth from Luxor hotels, and the Abu Simbel trip from your hotel in Aswan, an early start because the road takes 3.5 to 4 hours each way. Your pickup time is confirmed for your departure.

Where a tour page names a meeting point instead of hotel pickup, that is where the day starts. If your accommodation is an apartment or a guesthouse on a back street, confirm the exact pickup spot with Sawa before the day. Be ready ten minutes early: a shared departure cannot hold the vehicle for one latecomer.

Airport transfers are separate. Day tours start at hotels, not terminals, so an early-morning landing does not plug into a morning Giza pickup: if you are flying in, including from the Red Sea, sleep in Cairo the night before. And no day tour includes your visa: check Egypt's official e-visa portal before you fly.

Entry tickets: what's covered and what costs extra

Entrance tickets for the sites named in the itinerary are included; interiors and celebrity tombs are not. On Giza Uncovered, the Giza Plateau entrance ticket, the panorama viewpoint and the Great Sphinx are covered, but going inside the Great Pyramid of Khufu is bought separately. On Luxor in Depth, entrance tickets for the itinerary sites (Luxor Temple, Karnak, the Valley of the Kings, the Valley of the Queens, the Colossi of Memnon and the Temple of Hatshepsut) are covered; the special tombs (Tutankhamun's tomb, KV62, and Nefertari's, QV66) are never included and need their own tickets, and Nefertari's tomb has been closed since March 2024.

One nuance to remember: the included list covers named sites only. If a museum or temple is not on the itinerary, its ticket is not in the price either, which is what "optional activities" means in the exclusion list. For current monument prices, use the Ministry's site, egymonuments.gov.eg. Prices checked in November 2026: EGP 700 (about €12) for the Giza Plateau, EGP 1,500 (about €25) for the Great Pyramid interior since January 2025, and EGP 700 (about €12) for KV62; confirm them before you budget.

The extras worth budgeting for

Beyond the tour price, the extras most travellers pay for are the Great Pyramid interior, a camel ride at Giza, drinks across a hot day, and tips for the guide and driver. None is required (the Sphinx looks the same from ground level), but a day that starts at €29 can end with a fair stack of small payments, so carry cash in small notes. Five mistakes to avoid:

  • Reading only the included list. The not-included list decides your real budget; each Sawa tour page carries both before you reserve.
  • Expecting lunch on a half-day tour. Giza Uncovered's list says meals are not mentioned; check each tour.
  • Booking a tour for your landing day. Pickup is from hotels, so an early arrival plus a morning tour rarely works.
  • Assuming "tickets included" means every tomb. Standard sites yes; interiors and special tombs no.
  • Carrying no cash. Tips, drinks and optional extras are paid on the day, and small payments are easiest in cash.

How to check inclusions on a Sawa departure

Every tour page on Sawa Tours carries an included and a not-included list, so you can compare a €29 half-day and a €75 full day on facts rather than adjectives. Tours run as shared departures on a fixed catalogue: one date, one guide, at most eight travellers, at a price fixed per traveller with no solo surcharge on day tours. Reserving a seat is free, needs no card, and nothing is charged before the date confirms. The date confirms (the GoAhead) when four travellers have reserved it; then a 10% deposit is due by a secure payment link from Online Era (General Sales Agent licence 32241), and the balance is due 2 days (48 hours) before departure. Charges are in euros. A forming date has until 7 days before the tour to reach four; if it does not, it is cancelled, nothing is charged, and another date is suggested. Cancelling at least 48 hours before departure is a full refund, deposit included; under 48 hours means the 10% deposit is retained. The details are in the terms and FAQ. Browse all tours and packages or see forming departures, or read how the GoAhead works.

The verdict on what's included

Read the not-included list before the included one: it tells you what your day will really cost. Guide, transport, hotel pickup and the standard entry tickets are safe assumptions where the page lists them; tips, drinks, camel rides and special interiors are not. Next step: open the full tour list, compare the two lists on a date that suits you, then reserve a free seat on Giza Uncovered.

Islam Hussein is an Egyptologist guide who has worked in Egyptian tourism since 1993, first as a guide and then running an agency, and the founder of Sawa Tours. More about Sawa Tours.

faq.q: What is usually included in an Egypt day tour?
faq.a: A licensed guide, an air-conditioned vehicle with driver, hotel pickup and drop-off, and entrance tickets to the sites named in the itinerary. Some full-day tours add lunch at a local restaurant, and some list taxes and service charges. Anything not on the list, such as tips, drinks, camel rides and special-tomb tickets, you pay for separately.

faq.q: Do Egypt tours include hotel pickup?
faq.a: Usually yes: hotel pickup and drop-off are listed on the Sawa day tours we checked, at no extra charge, including hotel pickup in Aswan for the Abu Simbel trip. Your pickup time is confirmed for your departure; where a page names a meeting point instead, start there, and confirm your exact pickup spot if you are staying somewhere hard to find.

faq.q: Is lunch included on Egypt day tours?
faq.a: It depends on the tour, so read the list. On Sawa's pages, Aswan to Abu Simbel and the Grand West Bank list a local-restaurant lunch en route as included, Giza Uncovered says meals and drinks are not mentioned, and Luxor in Depth mentions lunch in the itinerary but not in its lists, so check the departure page. Drinks, including bottled water, are normally paid separately, so carry a little cash anyway.

faq.q: Are entrance tickets included in the tour price?
faq.a: Tickets to the sites named in the itinerary are included; tickets to interiors and special tombs are not. On Giza Uncovered the plateau ticket is covered but entering the Great Pyramid of Khufu costs extra; on Luxor in Depth the itinerary sites are covered but Tutankhamun's and Nefertari's tombs are listed as not included.

faq.q: How much should I tip on a day tour in Egypt?
faq.a: Tips are not included in the tour price, and most Sawa not-included lists name gratuities. Amounts are a personal decision and guides disagree: 2026 guides quote about EGP 100 to 200 per person (about €2 to €3) for a group guide on a full-day tour, with higher figures from operators who quote in dollars. Pay in cash, directly to the guide or driver.

faq.q: What happens if a Sawa departure doesn't fill?
faq.a: Nothing is charged until a date reaches four travellers (the GoAhead). A forming date has until 7 days before the tour to reach four; if it does not, it is cancelled, nothing is charged, and another date is suggested. Once a departure is confirmed, the tour keeps running for the others if a traveller drops out or does not pay, and the price stays fixed for everyone.
